messages:
sophie: Quick note — I'm prototyping a 'Failover Policy Editor' in the console so teams can reorder and tune model fallback lanes without PRs. current flow is too slow for on-call tweaks.
sophie: goal: allow reorder, set circuit-breaker thresholds, attach quota-signal predicates, and preview expected route behavior for a sample request.
raj: love it. +1 for showing realtime cb metrics next to each lane so you can see 'why' a lane will be skipped. :eyes:
ash: do we have per-route CB open/close events in telemetry today? last I checked we only emit host-level counts.
maria: we emit per-model cb events but not annotated with route-match metadata. we could add route_id -> cb_event label. small change in runtime.
taylor: UI idea: drag handles + inline JSON editor for advanced rules, plus a small 'simulate' button that runs a sample header/payload through the routing engine and shows chosen path(s).
sophie: simulation is crucial. also want to expose a 'quota_threshold' that behaves like: if remaining_quota < X then deprioritize lane. avoids hitting tenant burst quotas and triggering failures.
jen-ux: mockup coming later today — thinking a compact card list for lanes with pills for: priority, cb_state, quota_signal, last_5xx_rate.
raj: telemetry hook proposal: emit route_decision events with fields: route_id, matched_headers, chosen_lane, fallback_stack, cb_state_at_eval, quota_snapshot. that'll make the simulation & audit traces accurate.
maria: example policy snippet for runtime (proto/JSON):
```json
{
  "route_match": {"path": "/v1/generate", "method": "POST", "header": {"x-tenant": "regex:^acme-.*$"}},
  "lanes": [
    {"name": "redwood-prod", "priority": 100, "cb_threshold_rps": 1200, "quota_threshold_pct": 10},
    {"name": "redwood-lowcost", "priority": 200, "cb_threshold_rps": 800, "quota_threshold_pct": 5},
    {"name": "open-source-fallback", "priority": 300, "cb_threshold_rps": 400, "quota_threshold_pct": 0}
  ],
  "soft_failover": {"cooldown_sec": 30, "prefer_lower_cost": true}
}
```
ash: that looks good. two asks: 1) include header_override when switching lanes so downstream gets a trace header (X-RW-Route) and 2) emit a short reason code when a lane is skipped (e.g., QB_LOW, CB_OPEN, CAPACITY_CONSTRAINED).
sophie: yes to both. reason codes will help on-call and also feed alerts/SLIs.
taylor: for console UX: show reason code as a tooltip on the lane card (yellow for soft_skip, red for hard_skip). also allow quick edits: set 'prefer_lower_cost' toggle.
raj: question about rollout: should the editor create a policy version and require a canary rollout? we already have rollouts for models. I'd prefer a staged rollout with per-tenant targeting.
maria: backend: policy versioning is straightforward — store policy blobs with tags. runtime can do version pinning per-tenant. canary field could be: rollout_percent and tenant_allowlist.
jen-ux: will include a tiny 'preview rollout' map showing sample tenants affected.
deploy-bot: feature-flag created: console.failover_editor; rolled out to beta accounts. :shipit:
sophie: next steps — raj to add route_id labels to CB events, maria to add route_decision telemetry, taylor/jen-ux to iterate mockups, I'll draft API contract for the editor. anyone object?
ash: no objections. happy to help with backend perf testing once we have schema.
raj: I'll open a tiny runtime PR to attach route_id to cb events and add reason_code enums.
sophie: thanks all — putting an entry in the eng-platform backlog and tagging owners.
